items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 40-year-old female came to your clinic complaining of bilateral protrusion of her eyes. She gave a history of excessive sweating and weight loss. Examination revealed lid lag and lid retraction.

options.a: Hyperthyroidism is more in females than males.
options.b: Thyroid eye disease is improved by taking radioactive iodine.
options.c: Cornea is never affected in thyroid eye disease.
options.d: Glucocorticoids may be used in treatment of thyroid eye disease.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 60-year-old male patient came complaining of bilateral proptosis with impairment of central vision of his left eye and defective color vision especially red and green. Examination revealed afferent pupillary defect of his left eye. Vision was 6/24 in right eye and 2/60 in left eye. He gave history of thyroid eye disease.

options.a: Color vision affection denotes patient should be referred to an ophthalmologist rapidly.
options.b: The cause of proptosis may be due to accumulation of fats in extraocular muscles only.
options.c: CT scan of orbit is a main tool in diagnosis.
options.d: Dry eye never occurs in thyroid eye disease.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 67-year-old female came to emergency room with severe headache, vomiting and protrusion of her right eye. Examination revealed bilateral papilledema. The patient gave history of radical mastectomy for cancer breast followed by chemotherapy 2 years ago.

options.a: Proptosis may be due to metastasis.
options.b: Protrusion of the eye may be due to chemotherapy.
options.c: Bilateral papilledema denotes a localized tumor in right eye.
options.d: CT scan of the globe is recommended.

options.c: Treatment is oral and topical antibiotics.

options.c: Possible cause is blockage of orifices of Meibomian glands.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A mother came to ophthalmic clinic with her 2 years child complaining of drooping of upper left eyelid compared to his right eye. Examination revealed absence of lid crease in his left upper lid.

options.a: Normally the upper lid covers 4mm of the cornea.
options.b: Degree of ptosis is judged by lid margin-corneal reflex distance (MRD).
options.c: Congenital ptosis is the most common cause.
options.d: Dystrophy of orbicularis muscle is the cause of ptosis.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 65-year-old diabetic male came to ophthalmology clinic complaining of blurred vision and drooping of his right upper lid and deviation of his eye outwards. Examination revealed dilated pupil and paralytic divergent squint.

options.a: Examination of extraocular muscles is essential.
options.b: Third nerve palsy may be the cause.
options.c: Horner syndrome is the main diagnosis.
options.d: Apraclonidine test is essential in diagnosis.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 35-year-old female patient came to clinic complaining of foreign body sensation and lacrimation. Examination revealed a row of lashes misdirected and rubbing against the cornea. She was diagnosed trachoma 3 years ago.

options.c: Management is by mucous membrane graft.
options.d: Management by antibiotic eye drops is the main line for this patient.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 45-year-old female came complaining of epiphora and bad cosmetic appearance of her lower lid. She gave a history of chemical burn to her skin below lid in the last 6 months. Examination showed exposure of palpebral conjunctiva.

options.b: Shortening of skin is not the cause.
options.c: Treatment is by a skin graft.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 70-year-old male came complaining of lacrimation, inability to close the lids while sleeping. Examination revealed keratitis and ulcer at lower part of cornea.

options.a: The commonest cause is Bell's palsy.
options.b: The eyes roll down during sleep.
options.c: Treatment is artificial tears and temporary lateral tarsorrhaphy.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 30-year-old female came to ophthalmic clinic with upper lid diffuse edema after putting a new type of cosmetics. The lid was red hot and swollen.

options.a: Lid edema may be due to mosquito bite.
options.b: Bilateral lid edema maybe due to renal or cardiac diseases.
options.c: Acute hordeolum never causes lid edema.
options.d: Lid edema cannot happen due to spread of fluid from scalp or face.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A patient came complaining of left epiphora. She gave history of an accident where left lid was wounded and repaired at the medial canthus. Globe was normal.

options.a: Possible cause of this condition is congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction.
options.b: Fluorescein dye disappearance test is helpful in diagnosis.
options.c: Punctal or canalicular obstruction may be the cause.
options.d: Treatment with artificial tears is the only line for treatment.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 62-year-old male came to ophthalmology clinic complaining of swelling at inner canthus. The swelling was painful and tender. Regurge was absent.

options.a: Most probable diagnosis is chronic dacryocystitis.
options.b: Staphylococcus aureus or streptococcus may be the cause.
options.c: Treatment by DCR is the main line of treatment.
options.d: Predisposing cause to that condition is cataract surgery.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 58-year-old female came to outpatient clinic complaining of tearing and recurrent mucoid discharge. On examination a swelling below the medial palpebral ligament was detected. Regurge test was positive.

options.a: Positive regurge test is of no value in diagnosis.
options.b: Recurrent conjunctivitis is one of the complications of the disease.
options.c: Most probable diagnosis is acute dacryocystitis.
options.d: Inflammation of lacrimal sac is due to nasolacrimal duct obstruction.

items.chapter: The protective system of the eye
items.stem: A 48-year-old female came complaining of discomfort, irritation and foreign body sensation both eyes. She gave a history of arthritis and dry mouth. On examination there were tear film debris.

options.b: Deficiency in aqueous tears is the main cause.
options.c: Schirmer's test is of value in diagnosis.

items.stem: A farmer came to outpatient clinic complaining of burning sensation, excessive tears and discomfort which increases while working outdoors in sun. On examination conjunctival scarring, PTDs and Arlt’s line were detected.

options.a: Cause of this condition is Sjogren's syndrome.
options.b: Mucin deficiency is the main cause.
options.c: BUT (tear film break up time) is not essential in diagnosis.
